title: Company Operations Process Crosswalk & Template Kit
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Overview

This page consolidates company-wide policies and operational processes into a single crosswalk, with ready-to-use templates for common actions: access & permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. Its primary goal is to reduce ambiguity by: (1) clarifying ownership and approvals for routine decisions, (2) providing step-by-step procedures for common tasks, and (3) publishing canonical templates and checklists that teams can copy.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood corporate and product teams unless a separate customer- or regulation-specific exception exists.
- Does not replace role-specific runbooks (e.g., SRE incident runbooks); it provides the governance layer and standardized forms.

Document structure

1) Roles & ownership matrix
2) Access & permissions: request, review, audit
3) Change management: standard and emergency paths
4) Data management: classification, handling, retention
5) Procurement & expenses: thresholds, PO and card usage
6) Vendor management: onboarding and risk checklist
7) Travel policy: booking, approvals and reimbursement
8) Templates and examples (copyable blocks)
9) Governance and review cadence

1) Roles & ownership matrix

- Document owner: People Ops (process maintenance, templates).
- Access approvals: Team Manager -> Service Owner -> Security for sensitive resources.
- Procurement approvals: Requester -> Manager -> Finance for up to $10k; Manager + Finance -> Legal for > $10k.
- Change approvals: Service Owner -> Change Approver (SRE/Platform) -> Production Change Window.
- Vendor onboarding: Procurement lead -> Security -> Legal signoff -> Contracting.

Owners and definitions

- Requester: person initiating request (access, purchase, travel).
- Service Owner: team designated owner for a given service or dataset.
- Approval Authority: role with explicit delegation to approve (manager, finance partner, security reviewer).

2) Access & permissions

Principles

- Principle of least privilege: grant minimum permissions for a defined period.
- Time-bound access: temporary access must have an expiry and be audited.
- Segregation of duties: no single person should perform production change and approval concurrently unless designated as emergency on-call.

Standard access request flow (non-sensitive resources)

1. Requester files an Access Request via the Access Portal (or Workday form for people & payroll access). Required fields: requester, resource name, reason, duration, intended actions.
2. Team Manager reviews, confirms business justification, and either approves or requests changes.
3. System Owner enforces configuration change and records grant in the access registry.
4. Automated audit job generates monthly access snapshot; owners must attest quarterly.

Access approval matrix (simplified)

| Resource type | Approver | Typical duration | Extra controls |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Non-prod compute (dev/test) | Team Manager | 30 days | Token/SSH rotation on handoff |
| Production application access | Service Owner + SRE | 14 days | MFA mandatory, session recording |
| Sensitive dataset (PII/PHI) | Security + Data Owner | 7 days | Data access agreement, DLP enabled |
| Cloud infra (IAM role) | Infra Owner + Security | 1 day | Just-in-time (JIT) + ephemeral creds |

Access review cadence

- Quarterly attestation by owners for all production and sensitive access.
- Automated reminders at 21, 14, and 7 days before temporary grants expire.
- Emergency access (see change mgmt) requires post-hoc audit within 72 hours.

3) Change management

Change categories

- Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized items with documented rollback (e.g., config tweaks, capacity scaling).
- Normal change: larger changes requiring approval and scheduling (e.g., model rollout, infra upgrades).
- Emergency change: required to remediate incidents and restore service quickly.

Standard change process

1. Submit change request in Change Tracker (title, impact, rollback plan, owner, start/stop window).
2. Change Approver (SRE lead) reviews risk and schedules during a change window.
3. Pre-change checklist completed (backups, runbook, monitoring set).
4. Execute change and mark status.
5. Post-change verification and update the runbook.

Emergency change flow

1. During an incident, the incident commander may declare emergency change.
2. Implement fix with minimal required approvers (on-call, service owner).
3. File retrospective and change ticket within 24 hours.
4. Conduct post-implementation review and root cause analysis (RCA) within 7 days.

Rollback criteria and metrics

- Automatic rollback if error rate exceeds 5% for 5 minutes or latency increases 3x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Owners must define service-level rollback triggers in the change request.

4) Data management

Classification labels

- Public: intended for public consumption. No controls required beyond retention policy.
- Internal: Redwood-internal; retention per team defaults.
- Confidential: business-sensitive (e.g., financial plans, contracts). Access restricted to business need.
- Sensitive (PII/PHI): regulated; must follow encryption, approved processing, and minimization.

Handling and storage rules

- All Sensitive data must be stored in approved encrypted stores; keys managed by KMS.
- Export of Sensitive data requires Data Owner signoff and documented business justification.
- De-identification preferred before analysis; use tokenization or irreversible hashing when possible.

Retention and deletion

- Default retention: 36 months for Internal and Confidential unless business reason.
- Sensitive data: follow legal/regulatory retention schedules (e.g., payroll/tax data per country law).
- Data deletion requests: owner completes deletion ticket; infra runs deletion within SLA (standard: 10 business days).

Data access request form (example fields)

- Dataset identifier
- Purpose of access
- Duration requested
- Export required (yes/no)
- Reviewer comments

5) Procurement & expenses

Principles and thresholds

- Use company purchasing card for business travel and low-value purchases (< $2,500) when approved by manager.
- Purchase orders (POs) required for vendor spend > $10,000.
- Capital expenses and multi-year contracts require Finance and Legal review.

Procurement flow (standard vendor purchase)

1. Requester submits Procurement Request form with business justification and budget code.
2. Manager approves. If > $10k, Finance assigns procurement lead and Legal is notified.
3. Procurement lead obtains quotes (if applicable), negotiates terms, and requests Legal review.
4. Once contract executed, Procurement issues PO and informs requester.

Expense report guide (high-level)

- Submit receipts within 30 days of transaction.
- Cardholders must reconcile monthly.
- Meal per diem: $75 USD/day domestic; receipts required for single-meal transactions above $75.
- Lodging: economy or standard business class; exceptions require manager pre-approval.

PO template (copyable snippet)

{
  "po_number": "PO-XXXX-YYYY",
  "vendor_name": "Vendor, Inc.",
  "description": "Software subscription (annual)",
  "amount": "$XX,XXX",
  "billing_terms": "Net 30",
  "owner": "Team / Service Owner"
}

6) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist (minimal)

- Business justification and confirmed budget code.
- Security questionnaire completed (vendor risk level: low/medium/high).
- Data flow diagram if vendor will process company data.
- Contract with appropriate clauses (DPA, security, breach notification).
- Insurance verification and contact points.
- Kickoff meeting with SLAs and escalation contacts.

Vendor risk decisions

- Low risk: SaaS with no company data (e.g., public marketing tools). Procurement lead can complete onboarding.
- Medium risk: SaaS where company data is processed; Security review required.
- High risk: Vendors with access to PII/PHI or production systems; Requires Legal + Security + Procurement approval.

Periodic review

- High-risk vendors reviewed annually. Medium-risk every 18 months. Low-risk every 36 months.

7) Travel policy (quick reference)

Booking and approvals

- Domestic travel: manager approval required; use preferred booking partners for corporate rates.
- International travel: manager + People Ops approval; check visa and vaccination requirements.

Allowed expenses and limits

- Economy airfare standard; Premium economy allowable with manager pre-approval for flights > 8 hours.
- Ground transportation: rideshare or standard car service; receipts required.
- Per diem for meals as described in Expenses section.

Safety and duty of care

- Register travel with People Ops for international trips.
- Emergency contact and nearest embassy or consulate info must be provided for travel over 72 hours.

8) Templates and examples

- Access Request form (fields): requester, resource, justification, duration, owner, approver, business impact.
- Procurement Request form (fields): requester, budget code, vendor, estimated amount, justification, preferred vendor contact.
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (bulleted).
- Change Request template: title, owner, window, rollback, monitoring, test plan.
- Expense report sample line: {date, merchant, category, amount, project_code, receipt_link}.

9) Governance, metrics and review cadence

- Quarterly review cycle: People Ops maintains templates and collects feedback; Security and Finance run focused reviews on schedule.
- KPIs to track: average procurement lead time (target: < 10 business days), percent of access requests with time-bound expiry (target: 100%), number of emergency changes per quarter (target: trend down).
- Exceptions: Requests for permanent deviations must be logged as exceptions and approved by People Ops + relevant owner; exceptions are time-limited and reviewed semi-annually.

Appendices and links

- Access Portal: https://access.redwood.local (internal)
- Change Tracker: https://changelog.redwood.local (internal)
- Procurement Request Form: https://forms.redwood.local/procurement (internal)
- Data classification reference: confluence/security-and-compliance/data-classification

Change log

- 2024-05-20: Initial draft published.
- 2025-10-01: Updated procurement thresholds and vendor review cadence.

How to use these templates

- Copy the relevant template block into your team page and update service-specific fields (service owner, SLAs, contact points).
- Submit changes to this crosswalk via the PR template in People Ops (link above); all submissions will be reviewed and merged by People Ops and Security as appropriate.
